experiment: live bad-case pool: real questions through the demo product path, before and after fixes

grading.method: One grader agent per batch of 5-9 questions compared each live record with the verified gold answer and parsed source; an independent skeptic agent re-checked every grade and could change it.

runs.iteration2: scoping, compact context, citation repair, grounding, calculations, cross-fragment repair, one retry, review hardening (prompt v2)
runs.iteration3: + qualifier check, more quote repairs, no retry after an admitted gap, verifier-doubt rule (prompt v2, whose worked examples leaked B04's and A06's figures)
runs.after_fix: same code with prompt v2.1 (fictional worked examples); the final configuration

after_fix.D07: re-run once after a claim-side qualifier-check false positive (a year between qualifier and figure) was fixed; the first final-run record was discarded
after_fix.note: C02 in iteration3 was likewise re-run once after the verdict-doubt pattern 'assumed' was removed

typical_cases.root_cause: Each evidence unit was serialized three times with its full citation object; fragmented pages expanded ~10k characters of text to 100-400k, above the 100,000-character budget, so the request was refused before generation.
typical_cases.mitigation: Compact model view (each unit once as [id, page, kind, text]); provenance kept local; over budget drop the lowest-ranked passage that is not a company's or year's last; recheck the gate on packed passages.

typical_cases.root_cause: Sources contain NBSP, PDF ligatures and curly quotes; the model retyped them (spaces, letters, NUL plus hex), so the exact-substring check failed on correct drafts.
typical_cases.mitigation: Citation-repair pre-pass matches under NFKC/whitespace/dot-leader/hyphen normalization and rewrites the quote to the exact source span; the strict validator is unchanged.

typical_cases.root_cause: The parser stores one visual line as adjacent units; the model quotes across the boundary or cites the neighbouring evidence ID.
typical_cases.mitigation: Split a uniquely matching cross-unit quote into exact per-unit citations; rebind wrong IDs only to a unique exact match in the same report; one corrective retry for mechanical failures.

typical_cases.root_cause: One global vector search without entity resolution: aliases ('coke'), ambiguous tickers ('HD') and the more frequent company crowded out the other side.
typical_cases.mitigation: Query-scope resolver (names, aliases, typos, tickers, Chinese names); one exact FAISS search per company restricted to its reports; Top-5 reserves slots per company.

typical_cases.root_cause: Prompt v1 forbade derived values; margins and growth rates could not be quoted.
typical_cases.mitigation: Claims may carry a calculation object over cited operand cells; the application recomputes it in Decimal (scale constants only, sign/direction checked) and renders the formula.

typical_cases.failure_type: Relative period resolved to a stale year
typical_cases.root_cause: No resolution of 'last year' / 'current'; the model chose a year from its own knowledge and the typo 'starbuks' weakened matching.
typical_cases.mitigation: Resolve relative periods to each company's latest report, filter retrieval to it, and pass the interpretation to both models; fuzzy company matching.

typical_cases.failure_type: Undated question answered from an old report
typical_cases.root_cause: No period given and the reranker preferred older tables.
typical_cases.mitigation: Dedicated latest-report pool and two reserved latest-year slots for undated questions, plus a note to answer for and state the latest fiscal year.

typical_cases.failure_type: Historical figure presented as a forecast
typical_cases.root_cause: The generator relabelled FY2025 actuals as a 2027 projection and the verifier approved it while its reason noted the mismatch; no deterministic period check.
typical_cases.mitigation: Deterministic grounding of years, dates, numbers and companies against cited text; forecast intent and out-of-coverage notes; verdicts whose reason expresses doubt are rejected.

typical_cases.root_cause: Without year scoping, FY2024 reports outranked FY2023 ones and the verifier did not compare periods.
typical_cases.mitigation: Explicit years restrict each company's pool to that report; both models receive the requested period.

typical_cases.root_cause: Quotes were exact and numbers grounded, but the claim dropped 'Organic/non-GAAP' or 'including noncontrolling interests', or added 'excluding financing'; the verifier missed the basis change.
typical_cases.mitigation: Per-figure qualifier check: a qualifier attached to a quoted figure must stay with that figure in the claim; 'excluding' and similar narrowing words may only come from the sources.

replay.note: Iteration-2 released drafts replayed through the final checks

typical_cases.failure_type: Partial answer released with an admitted gap
typical_cases.root_cause: The generator answered the convenient part and wrote that the rest was not provided; the verifier passed it; a retry could delete the admission.
typical_cases.mitigation: Claims admitting missing evidence are rejected and that failure is never retried.

typical_cases.failure_type: Over-refusal by the calibrated confidence gate
typical_cases.root_cause: Raw reranker logits are uncalibrated; table rows and scoped pools score low even when the answer is correct.
typical_cases.mitigation: No default threshold; release is decided by exact references, deterministic grounding and the verifier; the 6.359375 gate stays an opt-in diagnostic.

typical_cases.root_cause: Prompt v2's worked examples were written from observed live failures: the scale example used A06's wrong sub-row figure (6,690) and the calculation example was B04's gold answer (Intel -31.4% from 54,228 and 79,024).
typical_cases.mitigation: Prompt v2.1 uses a fictional 'Example Corp'; prompts scanned for any question-pool figure; the final run repeated in full.

per_question.query: nvidia revenue 2024?

baseline.answer: NVIDIA's revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60,922 million. [^1]
baseline.failure_type: Bare year silently mapped to FY2024; FY-end caveat missing
baseline.root_cause: The value and its 'fiscal year 2024' label are correct, so this counts as a labelled interpretation. The query embedding for 'nvidia revenue 2024' pulled FY2024-labelled chunks almost exclusively, and nothing expands retrieval to the next fiscal year (FY2025). With all five top5 chunks from FY2024, the generator saw only one interpretation. Because no FY2025 evidence was in context and GENERATOR_SYSTEM has no fiscal-calendar instruction, it gave neither the Jan 28, 2024 period end nor the FY2025 alternative.

iteration1.answer: NVIDIA's consolidated revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, up 126% year on year. [^1][^2]

iteration2.answer:
NVIDIA's consolidated revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, up 126% year on year. [^1][^2]

NVIDIA's Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% year on year. [^3][^4][^5]

NVIDIA's Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $10.4 billion, up 15% year on year. [^6][^7][^8]
iteration2.failure_type: Ambiguity handled by one labelled interpretation; no period end or FY2025 note
iteration2.root_cause: The figures are correct and labelled 'fiscal year 2024', which meets the explicit-interpretation rule. Two things kept it short of the gold's fuller handling. (1) query_scope mapped bare '2024' only to the FY2024 label (requested_years=[2024], period_mode explicit). The scoped pool therefore excluded the FY2025 report, which spans Feb 2024 to Jan 2025, so the calendar-2024 reading could never be offered. (2) The scope note only permits a period end ('state the period end only if the sources show it'); it does not require one. No deterministic check asks for a period end on a calendar-ambiguous question, so the generator left out 'Jan 28, 2024' even though the p166 chunks in the top5 show it.

iteration3.failure_type: Verifier rejected a correct, exactly quoted claim with a made-up contradiction
iteration3.root_cause: The generator wrote one combined claim, '$60.9 billion, up 126% year on year', citing E40 'Consolidated $60.9 billion' and E41 'up 126% year on year'. Both quotes are exact, and claim_grounding passed. The verifier returned supported=false, saying 126% 'is inconsistent with the detailed segment growths'. That is false: 60,922/26,974 = +125.9%, and the 10-K itself says 'up 126% from a year ago' on p123. The verifier's own reason also admits 'The evidence does confirm $60.9 billion revenue and a 126% increase'. validate_semantic_verdict (answer_verification.py:1359) turns any unsupported verdict into unsupported_claim. _retry_feedback (generation.py:243) only retries deterministic failures, so a verifier rejection is final. Because both figures were in one claim (against prompt rule 10, 'One independently checkable fact per claim'), the disputed 126% also took down the correct $60.9B. Secondary issue: query_scope mapped '2024' only to the FY2024 label, so even a released answer could not mention that FY2025 ($130,497M, ending Jan 26, 2025) covers most of calendar 2024. An FY2024-labelled answer is still acceptable under the answer_or_clarify rubric.

after_fix.answer: NVIDIA's consolidated revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, up 126% year on year. [^1][^2]
after_fix.failure_type: Calendar-vs-fiscal ambiguity resolved to FY2024 without a period-end caveat
after_fix.root_cause: query_scope read the bare '2024' as the FY2024 label. Its note said: 'Calendar year 2024 was read as the fiscal year label FY2024... state the period end only if the sources show it'. It opened only the FY2024 pool, so the FY2025 interpretation (Feb 2024 to Jan 2025, $130,497M) never reached the generator. The released claim is numerically right and explicitly labelled 'fiscal year 2024', which meets the rubric's answer_or_clarify bar. It falls short of the gold's ideal: the period end appeared in top-5 chunks c369/c371 ('Year Ended Jan 28, 2024') but the note only permits stating it, so the generator left it out. The diagnostic gate would have accepted (max 6.527 >= 6.359).

per_question.query: walmart diluted EPS went from $4.27 in FY23 to $1.91 in FY24?? did earnings really drop that much or am I comparing the wrong numbers

baseline.failure_type: Generator adopted the false premise despite restated evidence in context
baseline.root_cause: The top5 put the FY2024 report's split-adjusted FY2023 EPS of $1.42 (E2), plus the FY2025 report's $1.42 (E16), next to the FY2023 report's pre-split $4.27 (E9). The generator drafted 'Diluted EPS ... was $4.27 in fiscal 2023 and $1.91 in fiscal 2024, indicating a significant drop'. It cited E2, whose quoted sentence itself gives FY2023 = $1.42, and E9. It mirrored the user's comparison instead of reporting the restatement conflict, against GENERATOR_SYSTEM's 'same metric/basis' and 'Refuse if ... conflicting' rules. The verifier correctly rejected the draft ('...comparing $4.27 to $1.91 is misleading'). That blocked an unsafe answer, but no premise-correcting answer was ever attempted. The stock-split explanation was never retrieved, because the dense query matched EPS/net-income MD&A prose rather than the Note 1 split paragraph. The non-comparability could still have been stated from E2/E16 alone.

iteration1.answer: Walmart's diluted EPS was $4.27 for fiscal 2023 and $1.91 for fiscal 2024. This indicates that earnings did not drop from $4.27 in FY23 to $1.91 in FY24, but rather the $4.27 figure and $1.91 figure pertain to different fiscal years as reported. [^1][^2]

iteration2.failure_type: Under-cited cross-report claim rejected by deterministic grounding on both attempts
iteration2.root_cause: Attempt 1 failed with claim_number_not_in_evidence because claim 0 said 'not $4.27' while citing only E2 (FY2024). That rejection was correct and useful, since attempt-1 claim 1 also wrongly said $4.27 'corresponds to an older fiscal year'. _retry_feedback (generation.py:251-256) names only the reason code and the claim index, not the failing token, and it does not tell the model to cite every unit a claim relies on. In the retry, claim 1 ('...$4.27 ... appears in the fiscal 2023 report but contradicts the fiscal 2023 EPS in the fiscal 2024 report...') cited only E9, the FY2023 chunk, and that chunk text contains no '2024'. check_claim_grounding (answer_verification.py:1135-1142) accepts a year only if it is a cited report's fiscal year or appears in the cited passages. The 4th of 5 year tokens (2024) failed that test. The check worked as specified: the statement about the FY2024 report rests on E2, which claim 1 did not cite. The defect is the generator splitting a cross-report comparison into single-citation claims, combined with feedback that does not guide the fix. Only one retry is allowed, so the pipeline abstained before the verifier ran. Even a passing draft would have been only partially correct, because the split was never retrieved and the draft called the gap a 'discrepancy' without explaining the 3-for-1 restatement.

iteration3.answer: Walmart's diluted net income per common share (EPS) attributable to Walmart was $1.91 for fiscal 2024 and $1.42 for fiscal 2023 according to the Walmart 2024 annual report, while the Walmart 2023 annual report states diluted EPS was $4.27 for fiscal 2023, indicating you are comparing diluted EPS based on different fiscal years and possibly different reporting or restatement bases. [^1][^2]
iteration3.failure_type: Premise correction incomplete; split disclosure never retrieved
iteration3.root_cause: The query is about EPS numbers and never says 'split', so dense retrieval ranked EPS and results paragraphs highest. None of the five split-disclosure passages entered the 20-candidate pool. With only the two conflicting EPS sentences in context, the generator followed the second half of prompt rule 8 ('give both values with their report years'). It did not follow the first half ('say the premise is not supported'), and gave a vague, partly misleading reason: 'different fiscal years', which is not the issue, and 'possibly ... restatement'. It never stated the like-for-like rise from $1.42 to $1.91. The verifier set answers_question=true, although its prompt requires a false premise to be 'corrected rather than adopted'. It also accepted the claim with the speculative reason 'likely before restatements'. _VERDICT_DOUBT does not match 'likely' or 'possibly', which I confirmed by running the regex on the verifier text.

after_fix.failure_type: Generator stated a figure without citing its source; split evidence never retrieved
after_fix.root_cause: check_claim_grounding runs each rule across all claims and the first failure wins (period checks before number checks). Attempt 1, claim 1 cited E9 (FY2023 report) but said 'revised to $1.42 in the fiscal 2024 report' and invented a 'prior reporting standard or non-GAAP' explanation. Year 2024 is not in E9, so the reason was claim_period_not_in_evidence. Claim 0 of attempt 1 already contained an ungrounded '$4.27' while citing only E2, but the feedback never named it because the period rule fired first. The retry feedback said 'a claim that compares two reports must cite a unit from each'. The retry dropped claim 1 but kept 'rather than a drop from $4.27' in a claim citing only E2, so grounding failed: 'number 3 of 3 ... does not occur in the cited evidence'. No retry remained. The grounding check worked as designed; the defect is that the generator did not co-cite E9, which was in context. Even if released, the draft would have been only partially correct: it calls the true pre-split $4.27 'incorrect' and never explains the Feb 23, 2024 3-for-1 split, because retrieval surfaced no split chunk.

The generator also converted 6,690 million to '$6.690 billion', a calculated value GENERATOR_SYSTEM forbids. Oracle's consolidated statement of operations for the year ended May 31, 2024 shows research and development expenses of $8,915 million. [^2]
